scope: Read-only review of candidate diff and actual app/worker failure cleanup path; no generalized tests or additional replay launched.

findings.issue: Application add catch sends remove for the just-failed new row, but World.add already removed it. Unconditional remove resets restored survivor contact history and reports.
findings.resolution: Candidate remove now returns immediately when removed.length is zero; verified in reviewed source.

reviewConclusions: Constructor collection and default initialize path retain original physical arithmetic/order; preparedSeed adds an independent copy only.
Prepared seed is taken after ClothSolver seam welding and pin selection, with solver particle indexing rather than display vertex indexing.
Only explicit successful add enters fromPreparedSeeds restart; no normal step path, material/rest/mass/thickness or acceptance limit was modified.
Initialize checkpoints p/v/old/initial/saved, garment clocks, edge/bend kernel arrays and physical World reports before contact reset.
On initialization failure, old arrays and reports are restored before contact checkpoint restore; outer add catch removes/releases only the new row.
Contact pending references remain valid because surviving row position arrays retain their identity and are restored in place.
Body query cache invalidation is an execution change; static body geometry and acceleration data are retained.
Nonexistent remove is now a physical no-op, preserving rollback through the actual UI cleanup sequence.
limits: Awaiting original same-sequence three-lane final result and targeted candidate rollback/redress regression.
Allocator high-water/reuse/free-byte accounting can change after a failed allocation/add attempt and is not asserted to roll back.
Node versus Chrome observed rendered checkpoints are not all byte-identical; direct Chrome binding remains separate from strict same-runtime lane comparison.
